note: Issue 388, patrons.md section 8. The window the whole patron game closes through: his final loyalty banks permanently when he goes, so these six months are the last chance to move it - and the PC is meant to know it TO THE MONTH. patron_leaving had been emitted since #283 and read by nothing, so the deadline the doc designed as actionable was a number in a log. The letter names the date and says plainly that business continues, because a man who stopped trading the month he gave notice would make the window worthless rather than valuable.

body.text: I am going home. Not immediately — I sail in {param:leaves} months, and I shall say so in every letter between now and then so that neither of us can pretend to have forgotten.
It is nothing you have done. My affairs want me and I have put them off twice already. One reaches an age where the putting-off costs more than the going.
Nothing changes until I sail. I shall trade as before, ask as before, and be as useful as I have been.
Nothing changes until I sail, which I say as a courtesy and not as an encouragement.

When I am back at court I shall be asked about you. I mention it not as a threat — I am in no position to threaten anybody from a chair in Westminster — but because you should know the question will be put, and that I shall answer it honestly.
When I am back at court I shall be asked about you, and I shall answer honestly. I would think about that, in your place.
There is nothing to answer here. I am telling you the date, which is more than most men get.
